payload.name: v0.9.0
payload.body: ## Overview This release adds OCP FP8 E4M3 quantization support, a new `flash_attn_ext_rows` op that makes the unified KV cache efficient for multi-sequence inference, and a generic batched tensor copy API. Four new architectures are supported (Clover, Limite, Metis-1.6 and Mistral Large 4), audio generation and transcription expand with Chatterbox TTS, Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe and predefined Pocket TTS voices, and the Gemma 4 E2B/E4B models get major prefill optimizations. `ggml` is updated to v0.29.0, bringing FP8 E4M3, flash attention rows, NCCL-based multi-node tensor parallelism and performance work across the CPU, CUDA, SYCL, Metal, Vulkan, OpenCL and Hexagon backends. The server and UI receive a round of fixes and refinements. ### Highlights - Quant: OCP FP8 E4M3 tensor type (saturating mode) with conversion helpers and a new ftype ([#27512](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/27512)) - llama: `flash_attn_ext_rows` - more efficient unified KV for multi-seq, restoring non-unified KV prefill performance ([#29510](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29510)) - ggml: batched tensor copy API (`ggml_backend_tensor_copy_n`/`set_n`/`get_n`) superseding the `_2d` API, implemented for Metal and CUDA ([#30881](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30881)) - For a 3rd year in a row, `llama.cpp` is a featured repo in the [Github Octoverse report](https://github.blog/news-insights/octoverse/octoverse-commits-pushes-reach-new-highs-in-2026-as-developers-build-with-agents/): ### API changes - llama.h: add `LLAMA_FTYPE_MOSTLY_F8_E4M3` ([#27512](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/27512)) - mtmd.h: add `MTMD_GEN_AUDIO_TYPE_CHATTERBOX` and `n_voices` to `mtmd_gen_audio_info` ([#30993](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30993)) - mtmd.h: add predefined-voice APIs: `mtmd_gen_audio_voice_name()`, `mtmd_gen_audio_get_voice()`, `mtmd_gen_state_set_ref()` ([#30993](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30993)) - mtmd.h: add `mtmd_bitmap_is_voice()` and `mtmd_gen_audio_read_tensor()` ([#30993](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30993)) - mtmd.h: add `MTMD_VIDEO_TEMPLATE_QWEN3VL` video prompt template ([#31619](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31619)) - server: `GET /props` reports the model's predefined TTS `voices`; the TTS endpoint accepts predefined voice names ([#30993](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30993)) - server: `/v1/responses` now merges `extra_params` (seed, min_p, ...) into the converted chat-completions response ([#30959](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30959)) ### New models - Clover-35B-A3B-Preview diffusion model, AR mode ([#31306](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31306)) - Limite 1B - Violetto ([#29433](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29433)) - Metis-1.6 (Praxis ~2.9B and Logos ~10.2B): hybrid Mamba-2 / GQA attention with fixed-depth recurrence and LatentMoE ([#31134](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31134)) - Mistral Large 4 ([#31376](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31376)) ### Core changes - gemma4: graph optimizations with massive prefill gains for E2B and E4B ([#31356](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31356)); create `token_embd` before the tied output in gemma3n and gemma4 ([#31394](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31394)) - LFM3: enable NVFP4 GGUFs ([#31608](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31608)), enable tensor split ([#31431](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31431)), quantize the audio codec decoder ([#31386](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31386)) - spec dec: save and restore MTP hidden state in context checkpoints ([#30141](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30141)) and record LFM3 layer inputs ([#31598](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31598)) - dflash: copy hidden features via device copies ([#31506](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31506)); qwen4exp: write the conv state tail without an intermediate cont ([#31443](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31443)) - model loading: reuse the tensor staging buffer and skip the direct-IO bounce buffer ([#31321](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31321)) - kv-cache: keep Hadamard rotation constants on the GPU ([#31073](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31073)) and fix attention tensor rotation in layers with shared KV ([#31406](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31406)) - kv-cache: never return 0 `kv_rows` for sequences without cells ([#31570](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31570)) and refuse rollbacks past the snapshots of the last ubatch ([#31368](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31368)) - Gemma4 MTP assistant: follow `ctx_other` devices and flash-attention setting ([#31635](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31635)); DSV4: remove simple batch splitting ([#31300](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31300)) - chat: strip the qwen3-coder think block with `reasoning_format none` ([#31380](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31380)) and end reasoning budget forcing on a prompt end tag ([#31374](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31374)) - chat: allow a constraint type after the gpt-oss final channel ([#31556](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31556)); common: fix `-hf` tag matching inside longer quant names ([#31620](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31620)) and bound control vector layer indices ([#31336](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31336)) - tools: reject mismatched shards in GGUF split merge ([#31579](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31579)), fix `imatrix --nextn` crash ([#31522](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31522)), fix `gguf-py` `np_roundf` dropping the sign ([#31310](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31310)) - vendor: miniaudio 0.11.26 ([#31459](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31459)) and cpp-httplib 0.64.0 ([#31400](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31400)); embed an app manifest in all Windows executables ([#31329](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31329)) ### Multi-modality changes - add Chatterbox TTS support ([#30993](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30993)) - add Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe support: offline transcription in 40 languages with prompt context and speaker attribution ([#31471](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31471)) - Pocket TTS: support predefined voices without voice cloning ([#31429](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31429)) - accurate support for the qwen3-vl video prompt format ([#31619](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31619)) - resize Gemma 4 images without letterbox padding ([#30922](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30922)) and fix InternVL CLS token order ([#30886](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30886)) ### Server changes - cap shared decision prefixes at the first output ([#30710](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30710)) - restore the speculative checkpoint for drafts longer than `n_rs_seq` ([#31350](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31350)) ### UI changes - add MCP group checkboxes in the tools settings ([#31303](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31303)) and request persistent storage on startup ([#31299](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31299)) - keep chats at the bottom until the reader scrolls up ([#31311](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31311)) and show the submit button when the input has content ([#31324](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31324)) - reveal the collapsed sidebar from its logo ([#31307](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31307)) and align alert dialog styling ([#31312](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31312)) - keep queued steering messages in their own conversation ([#31304](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31304)) and show an interrupted state for tool calls that never returned ([#31314](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31314)) - disable model deletion the server would refuse ([#31305](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31305)) and prefer a loading model in pre-selection ([#31326](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31326)) - add a Playwright harness for recording demo videos ([#31318](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31318)) and run local browser tests in installed Chrome ([#31596](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31596)) ### ggml changes - [v0.29.0](https://github.com/ggml-org/ggml/releases/tag/v0.29.0): ggml v0.29.0 adds an OCP FP8 E4M3 tensor type, a new `ggml_flash_attn_ext_rows` op where each query slice attends to its own list of K/V rows, a batched tensor copy API, and initial support for multi-node tensor parallelism through a new multi-process communicator interface. Core improvements include bounding tensor views by the bytes their strides reach, zero-copy GGUF export of host-buffer tensors, and `vm_allocate`-based allocations on Apple platforms. Performance work spans all major backends: new SVE kernels in the CPU backend, DPAS flash attention for quantized KV in SYCL, fused MoE MMQ in CUDA, faster MXFP4 mat-vec in Metal, split-K tuning in Vulkan, and a large expansion of quantized GEMM/GEMV coverage in OpenCL. The Hexagon backend gains support for several new ops, including the lightning indexer, top-k mask, conv2d and upscale. ## Assets **Nightly build:** title: langgenius/dify: v1.19.0 - Trace Your Workflows, Layer by Layer
summary:
**Dify 1.19.0 brings nested workflow tracing to your observability tools.** Follow a workflow into the Workflow Tools it calls, inspect the steps inside each invocation, and keep the LLM context alongside the execution tree. This release also makes Workflow Tools portable with App packages, adds Skill Hub automation, and makes Agent files easier to upload and preview. The bundled plugin daemon is upgraded to **0.6.14-local**. [Release highlights](#user-content-release-highlights) · [Upgrade guide](#user-content-upgrade-guide) · [Detailed changes](#user-content-detailed-changes) ## Release highlights ### Nested workflow tracing **See what happens inside a Workflow Tool, all the way down to its LLM calls.** Building on the Console drilldown introduced in 1.18.0, new external traces now include the persisted execution steps inside called Workflow Tools. Child steps appear beneath the Tool span that invoked them, preserving the hierarchy across nested and repeated calls. (#44673) ![Langfuse trace tree showing a workflow, nested Middle and Child Workflow Tools, and the selected LLM call with formatted prompts and responses](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langgenius/dify/dcfb52e62726c91b43db20f3c087acf285428df1/docs/assets/pr-44673-langfuse-nested-prompts.jpg) *From the outer workflow to a nested LLM call: the execution tree and formatted messages, together in Langfuse. Screenshot from [#44673](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/pull/44673).* - **Follow the hierarchy.** Expand called Workflow Tools to see their internal execution steps under the invoking Tool span. - **Understand each invocation.** Repeated calls and failures retain their place in the trace. - **Keep the LLM context.** Inspect formatted prompts and responses, token usage, and project, trace, and observation links. > [!NOTE] > **Your saved provider settings continue to work.** The richer hierarchy applies to new executions; historical traces are not backfilled. Independently nested workflow runs remain separate traces linked by parent identifiers. For rolling deployments, follow the [tracing queue transition](#user-content-upgrade-guide) below. ### Take Workflow Tools with your apps Export an app and bring the workflows behind its Workflow Tools with it. `.ifpkg` packages include those workflows at their bound versions, including transitive dependencies. Import reuses tools already in the destination workspace and recreates, publishes, and registers missing ones, remapping their references. (#44592) All Dify app exports now use **package format v2**, including apps without Workflow Tools. Existing v1 imports and explicit YAML export remain supported. See the [upgrade guide](#user-content-upgrade-guide) before importing new packages into older installations. (#45353) ### Upload together. Preview in place. Select or drop multiple Agent configuration files and upload them in parallel. Successful uploads are bound in one atomic batch, concurrent Composer saves preserve the latest files, and Prompt uploads keep the cursor position while inserting multiple references. (#44947) Read PDFs inline, inspect source files with syntax highlighting, and see when text has been truncated. Previews cover configured files, Skill members, and working-directory files, with a download action when a PDF cannot be loaded. (#45032, #45045)
See Agent file uploads and previews ![Inline PDF preview in Agent files, with the research brief and file list](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/22bafc75-c8f5-46fd-b7ba-c5097f9cffb6) *Read a PDF directly in the Agent file preview and switch between project files.* ![Agent batch upload dialog with a PDF, Python source file, and Markdown guidelines selected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5eafd0c1-f46d-4966-bbc0-e6cd5eacff02) *Select several files and upload them together.* ![Syntax-highlighted Python source in the Agent file preview](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1435fd23-7489-450a-a200-dbd81c1b588d) *Inspect source files with syntax highlighting and line numbers.*
## Developer spotlight **Manage workspace Skills through OpenAPI and difyctl.** Find and inspect Skills, export a draft or published version, import local files, and publish a new version from the command line. (#44941)
The six Skill commands | Command | Capability | | --- | --- | | `difyctl get skill` | List Skills, with keyword and tag filters. | | `difyctl describe skill` | Read details, the draft hash, and latest published version. | | `difyctl get skill version` | List published versions. | | `difyctl export skill` | Export the draft or a selected published version as ZIP. | | `difyctl import skill --files ` | Create a Skill or replace an existing Skill's draft from local files. | | `difyctl publish skill` | Publish the draft as a new version. |
These operations require an account caller, the corresponding workspace permissions, and Skills to be enabled. **Import does not publish.** Importing over an existing Skill is classified as destructive; the operation catalog and CLI help distinguish read, write, and destructive operations. (#44941, #45314, #44587) --- ## Upgrade guide > [!IMPORTANT] > **Read the upgrade guide before deploying.** Docker Compose now requires **v2.35.0 or later**. Preserve existing environment files, upgrade the Dify components together, and use the new tracing queue during rolling deployments. New App packages use format v2 and require a compatible destination importer. The bundled plugin daemon moves to **0.6.14-local**. **Compatibility and rollout** 1. **Back up first.** Retain the database, vector-store data, uploaded files, Agent snapshot/workspace storage, deployment secrets, and environment files. Use a maintenance window for a single-stack upgrade. 2. **Upgrade the components together.** Use matching `1.19.0` API, worker, web, Agent Backend, and Local sandbox images, with plugin daemon `0.6.14-local`. Keep the existing Local sandbox authentication token and any configured `PASSWORD_PEPPER` unchanged. If upgrading from before 1.18.0, also follow the [1.18.0 upgrade guide](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/releases/tag/1.18.0). 3. **Use Docker Compose 2.35.0 or later.** This is the minimum supported version for root `.env` overrides to take precedence when Compose resolves service defaults. Check your installed version with `docker compose version`. (#45359) 4. **Keep tracked defaults separate from local overrides.** Bundled `docker/envs/**/*.defaults` files load automatically. Customize a service through its matching local `.env` file, using the override path documented in the defaults file; root `docker/.env` holds deployment inputs and explicit overrides. Preserve existing `.env` files and edit them in place. Review accidentally empty assignments and values pinned by older template copies before upgrading. (#45359, #45376) 5. **Existing `shared.env` files remain supported.** Common API, worker, and Beat customizations now belong in `docker/envs/core-services/api-worker.env`. Compose still reads legacy `docker/envs/core-services/shared.env` first, then `api-worker.env`, so `api-worker.env` wins when both set conflicting values. Root `docker/.env` takes precedence over both. An unchanged copy of `api-worker.defaults` preserves existing `shared.env` customizations. See the [Docker configuration guide](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/blob/laipz8200/release-1.19.0/docker/README.md#review-configuration-after-an-upgrade). (#45376) 6. **Separate tracing queues during a rolling upgrade.** New tasks default to `OPS_TRACE_QUEUE=ops_trace_v2`; API, workers, and Beat must agree. Custom `CELERY_QUEUES`, `CELERY_WORKER_QUEUES`, or `--queues` lists must include the new queue. Keep old tracing workers on `ops_trace` until old producers and all their queued, active, reserved, scheduled, and retry work have finished. Do not purge the old queue or ask the new retired handler to export legacy messages. See the [tracing rollout guide](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/blob/laipz8200/release-1.19.0/api/providers/trace/README.md#rolling-upgrade-from-the-previous-pipeline). (#44673) 7. **Upgrade package destinations before importing new App packages.** New app packages always use format v2. Older importers, including builds with the earlier strict v2 rule, may reject them. Version 1 imports remain supported on 1.19.0. Explicit YAML export remains available, but does not carry bundled Workflow Tool dependencies. (#44592, #45353)
Deployment instructions · Docker Compose, source, and difyctl **Docker Compose** Once the 1.19.0 release tag and images are published, stop a single-stack deployment gracefully, switch to the release, retain and review configuration, then pull and start the new images: ```bash cd dify/docker docker compose stop -t -1 git fetch --tags git checkout 1.19.0 # Merge required configuration changes into existing env files here. docker compose pull docker compose up -d ``` Keep API startup migrations enabled (`MIGRATION_ENABLED=true`), or apply the full migration chain through your managed migration process before starting new workers. For rolling deployments, follow the separate tracing-queue sequence instead of mixing old and new consumers. Configure shared plugin credentials, `PLUGIN_DAEMON_KEY` and `PLUGIN_DIFY_INNER_API_KEY`, in root `docker/.env` so the daemon and its clients receive matching values. Ports, volume paths, profiles, and health-check scheduling also remain root configuration inputs. See the [Docker configuration guide](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/blob/laipz8200/release-1.19.0/docker/README.md#configure-dify). (#45359) **Source deployments** Use Python **3.13**, Node.js **24.22.1 or later in the 24.x line**, and pnpm **12.16.1**. pnpm no longer provisions Node.js for the workspace, so install the required Node.js runtime separately. (#44976, #45094) From the repository root: ```bash uv sync --project api --frozen uv run --directory api flask db upgrade pnpm install --frozen-lockfile ``` Rebuild the web application and restart API, worker, scheduler, and Agent services from the same release. Refresh the standalone Agent Backend's locked `server` dependencies when deploying it separately. **difyctl** Install the matching 1.19.0 client and use `difyctl help` to discover the current server catalog. Refresh installed agent skills with `difyctl install skills `. Workflow and Chatflow automation should use the revised `stop.run` operation; message-based apps use `stop.task`.
Database migrations and existing data Upgrading from 1.18.0 applies **six migration revisions**, ending at **`53c10126d551`**. Apply the complete chain through the normal migration runner. Operational changes to plan for include: - **Storage-cleanup indexes (`d7e9a1c3f502`).** Add reference indexes on `message_files.upload_file_id`, `workflow_node_execution_offload.file_id`, and `workflow_draft_variable_files.upload_file_id`. PostgreSQL creates them concurrently, but index construction still scans data and consumes I/O. Online upgrades reuse matching healthy indexes and reject conflicting or invalid definitions. Investigate an interrupted invalid build before retrying; do not drop healthy indexes as routine recovery. (#44982) - **Tracing configuration uniqueness (`53c10126d551`).** Keep one configuration per app/provider and add a unique index. When duplicates exist, the most recently updated row wins, with the ID breaking timestamp ties. Superseded rows are deleted; downgrading the index does not restore them. Retain a database backup. (#44673) - **Extraction changes affect newly processed content.** Re-import or re-index documents whose stored content was affected by the EPUB, EML, DOCX, CSV, Markdown, or Notion fixes. The repeated-PDF-preview fix prevents new duplicate assets for source uploads; it does not remove duplicates already stored. (#44836, #44953, #44905, #43505, #43434, #45053, #44684) - **Tracing history is not rebuilt.** Existing Agent trace-ledger data remains readable, but previously exported traces do not acquire the new nested spans. (#44673)
## Detailed changes
New capabilities · tracing, packages, and Skills **Tracing and provider integrations** - Consolidate delivery through the shared provider interface for Langfuse, LangSmith, Opik, Weave, Arize, Phoenix, Aliyun, MLflow, Databricks, and Tencent. Retryable exports resend the same trace unit with deterministic identifiers. (#44673) - Include called Workflow Tools' persisted execution frames in external exports, under their invoking Tool spans. Independently nested workflow runs remain separate traces linked by parent identifiers. (#44673) - Keep trace credentials write-only. Blank or omitted secrets preserve stored values; changing a destination host, endpoint, or URL requires entering its secrets again. (#44673) **Portable App packages** - Package the workflows behind called Workflow Tools, including transitive dependencies, with a default maximum of **20** bundled tool workflows. Missing destination tools are recreated and published; existing tools are reused. Creating missing tools requires tool-management permission and sufficient app quota. Packages needing DSL-version confirmation are rejected in this flow, and apps created before an import failure are cleaned up. (#44592) - Always emit format v2 for App packages, including nested packages and packages without Workflow Tools. This does not change the separate roster-Agent package format. (#45353) - Workflow and API tool IDs no longer become spurious `langgenius/` plugin dependencies during export. (#44592) **Skills and OpenAPI** - Export drafts or published Skill versions, import folders, and publish through account-authenticated workspace operations. An import with a Skill ID replaces that Skill's draft; the imported `SKILL.md` name must match. Optional `draft_hash` checks reject stale replacements, but use second-resolution timestamps and do not detect edits made within the same second. (#44941) - Skill import drops operating-system junk, rejects unsafe or duplicate paths, enforces file/size limits, reuses identical binary assets, and removes assets written by a failed import. Literal dashes inside Skill frontmatter are preserved. (#44941, #43602) - The operation catalog publishes each operation's effect, and CLI help displays it. Workflow/Chatflow stopping uses stored run ownership and state; unknown runs return `404`, and finished or otherwise non-stoppable runs return `409`. Message-app stopping keeps its task-ID semantics. (#44587, #45314) - Add the experimental `@dify/openapi-content-mapper` package for typed API calls and query helpers inferred from OpenAPI sources, with reusable schema/input/output types and opt-in contract-compatible type subpaths. This is development groundwork; these changes do not migrate production Console or Marketplace calls away from their existing clients. (#44627, #44915)
Improvements · editing, accessibility, performance, and operations - **Batch Agent file management:** multi-select and multi-file drop, parallel uploads, one atomic binding request, retry using cached upload IDs, and protection against stale Composer saves overwriting newly bound files. Existing single-file endpoints remain compatible. (#44947) - **More usable previews:** highlighted text, on-demand PDF rendering, stable open previews, and explicit truncated-text notices across Agent files, Skills, and working directories. (#45032, #45045) - **Direction and keyboard support:** synchronized locale direction, broader right-to-left layouts, date/time pickers integrated with forms and focus containment, visible labels retained in accessible names, and consistent read-only controls. (#44621, #43869, #44638, #44650, #44593, #44755, #44772, #44589, #45036, #45375) - **Safer editing dialogs:** deletion, rename, metadata, annotation, member-role, and plugin-setting dialogs preserve their sessions and drafts, keep pending actions open, and restore focus after completion. Repeated deletion submissions are blocked while a request is pending. (#44618, #44623, #44643, #44646, #44698, #44736, #44743, #44810, #44825, #44788, #44715, #44652, #44838, #44830) - **Clearer feedback:** field errors and persistent notices appear near the controls they concern, with shared alert presentation across apps, workflows, knowledge, billing, and Skills. Cloud billing uses localized prompts for retryable and action-specific errors. (#45151, #45264, #45266, #45267, #45268, #45192) - **Accurate Cloud quota displays:** distinguish unlimited counts from zero-capacity App Run and trigger quotas, and interpret reset dates as Unix seconds. Pricing display data no longer doubles as live usage limits. (#45117, #45115) - **Lower query overhead:** segment pages load child chunks and attachments in batches; new reference indexes support app storage cleanup. (#45050, #44982) - **Connection reuse:** Gunicorn's configurable keep-alive defaults to 10 seconds, reducing failures caused by reusing connections after the server's shorter idle window. (#44839) - **Docker configuration:** service and provider overrides now reach the relevant containers, database commands, health checks, and WebSocket settings. The generator creates only a missing root `.env`, leaving optional overrides under operator control. (#45359, #45376)
Security enhancements - **Workspace controls:** enabling or disabling provider models requires an owner or administrator. Email-availability checks require account admission. ([64fe95667b](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/commit/64fe95667b216dad6a44aa5ed4e45768f5672781), [76979a1e24](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/commit/76979a1e2421492ec34f852bc462ee4912643260)) - **Request-scoped cookies:** pooled SSRF clients retain response cookies only within the current outbound request and its redirects, preventing later requests from inheriting another request's cookies. (#44672) - **Dataset token scope:** resource access tokens can list only their explicitly bound active datasets; `include_all=true` cannot widen that scope. Legacy workspace Dataset API keys retain tenant-wide behavior without inheriting an injected owner's personal visibility filters. (#44840) - **App access settings:** importing DSL over an existing app preserves its Web App access mode, and converting an app inherits the source access mode. (#44700, #44857) - **Tracing secrets and egress:** configuration reads no longer return saved credentials, destination changes require secret re-entry, and provider traffic uses the shared outbound policy. (#44673) - **Dependency hardening:** update Authlib to 1.9.1, require LiteLLM 1.100.4 or later within its supported major version, move Agent Pydantic AI to 2.53.0 and Pillow to 13.0.0, update pypdf to 6.21.4, and refresh Werkzeug, GitPython, and other dependency fixes. The standalone Agent pins filelock 4.2.1; Docker build tooling updates uv to 0.13.4. These source updates do not claim to resolve every finding in external or Enterprise base images. (#44606, #44793, #44868, #44871, #44886, #45041, #45104, #45215, #45259, #45214, #45260)
Bug fixes · workflows, Agents, knowledge, APIs, and the web app **Workflows and execution** - Restore structured-output fallback for models without native support and preserve JSON booleans instead of converting them to strings. (#44962) - Honor configured file and file-list defaults across Studio, published apps, and API execution. Explicit clearing stays distinct from omission, reset conversations restore defaults, and saving file defaults no longer sends browser Blob objects that cause `415` errors. (#44780, #45042) - Preserve numeric zero in required Studio inputs and previews, and preserve both zero and false in opening statements. Non-object file-reference payloads fall back to the original reference instead of failing unexpectedly. (#45005, #44833, #45088) - Admit streaming Workflow and Chatflow requests only once against app concurrency limits, so a limit of one accepts the single active request. Terminal Chatflow events now stop the execution watchdog and release its retained context. (#45038, #45029) - Preserve caller identity for scheduled Agent file access, use the UTC clock for the Start node's `sys.timestamp`, and order weekly schedule previews by date. Webhook query/form numbers retain integer precision and reject non-finite values. (#44796, #44847, #44718, #44706) - Refresh available workflow nodes when availability changes, retain generated variables when applying a generated prompt, escape variable-search highlighting, and preserve prompt-editor focus when variable metadata refreshes. (#44769, #45274, #44625, #44791) - Request clear-canvas confirmation only when clearing a previously nonempty saved draft, and wrap long workflow error messages. (#45028, #45106) **Agents, tools, and Skills** - Persist refreshed OAuth credentials and serialize concurrent refreshes across tools and datasources, protecting rotating tokens and concurrent reauthorization. Temporary refresh failures return a temporary-unavailability response instead of incorrectly asking users to repair valid credentials. (#32195) - Reject late non-terminal events after an Agent stream has completed or been cancelled. Deduplicate plugin JSON output by content rather than formatting, and retain trailing partial action/thought prefixes in ReAct output. (#45080, #45297, #43353) - Stop serializing the entire prompt history into every Agent LLM gateway response chunk. Preserve request content, tool calls, multimodal content, usage, and quota settlement. (#45137) - Handle non-recording tracing parents and isolate concurrent Celery tracing contexts. (#44701, #44803, #45049) - Allow current Qwen flash models in Agent v2 and refresh suggested model patterns. Omit empty optional Agent variable inputs, and accept legacy comma-separated values for multiple-select tool parameters. (#44873, #44748, #45058) - Restore creator-based Agent edit permissions. Skill and snippet searches treat wildcard characters literally, and imported integration bundles retain their plugin icons. (#45040, #44922, #44708, #45112) **Knowledge and document processing** - Remove index entries written by a document that was deleted during indexing. Partial QA-segment updates preserve an omitted answer and its contribution to counts. (#44364, #44997) - Include documents missing a metadata key in negative metadata filters, honor explicit `top_k=0`, normalize blank legacy retrieval settings on read, and use keyword retrieval for Economy datasets in retrieval previews. (#44753, #42980, #45020, #44895) - Restore Notion page listing and file import, keep failed page loads retryable, and surface Notion database HTTP failures. (#45053, #44893) - Read EPUB chapters in declared order without extracting archive members to disk; preserve already-decoded EML text; identify DOCX images by relationship type; support numeric CSV column labels; and keep headings inside Markdown code fences intact. (#44836, #44953, #44905, #43505, #43434) - Reuse extracted PDF image assets for repeated previews of the same source upload. Restore Service API file-document creation/update when tenant context is missing or the original dataset creator has left. (#44684, #44972) - Include users' own maintained datasets in their lists. (#44795) **APIs, files, and SDKs** - Let MCP Chatflow generation commit its conversation session without a closed-transaction error. API-tool imports ignore non-method Swagger path keys. Suggested-question parsing retains brackets inside quoted questions, and missing citation resources return an empty list. (#44636, #44992, #44916, #43036) - Normalize remote Content-Type values, preserve detected media types for uploads accepted through “Other File Types,” and apply media-specific limits during remote-upload preflight. (#44677, #41292, #44273) - Report download HTTP failures instead of passing error pages to the plugin installer. Distinguish Squid-generated denial responses from upstream authentication errors, preserve GitHub import paths containing `blob`, and reject incompatible multipart file shapes consistently. (#44333, #44841, #44280, #44903) - The Node.js SDK accepts long knowledge-document text, handles CR/LF/CRLF SSE framing and a leading BOM, and accepts an empty pagination cursor as the first page. (#44679, #44263, #44265) - The PHP SDK serializes empty app inputs as JSON objects, avoids buffering streaming Workflow and text-to-audio responses, and sends `last_id` for conversation pagination while preserving its public method signature. (#44675, #44271, #44659) **Web app and workspace** - Keep newly created, user-maintained apps visible in Studio and preserve primary navigation across Console routes. Calculate log-period boundaries from the current date. (#44929, #44633, #45360) - Use navigable links in document menus, open publisher destinations in new tabs, and advance integration-tour steps without reloading the page. (#44694, #44808, #44934, #44944) - Respect Marketplace availability across template and plugin entry points and render emoji-ID icons in recommended cards. (#45009, #45027, #45066) - Preserve annotation editor drafts and voice-input focus, and add the Simplified Chinese account-deletion success email template. (#44810, #44825, #45169, #43504)
Environment variables and integration changes | Setting | Change in 1.19.0 | | --- | --- | | `OPS_TRACE_QUEUE` | New; defaults to `ops_trace_v2`. Shared by trace delivery/retries, Agent trace work, payload cleanup, and sandbox metering. API, workers, and Beat must agree. | | `OPS_TRACE_EXPORT_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | New; defaults to `6` total attempts for retryable trace exports. | | `ENABLE_TRACE_PAYLOAD_SWEEP_TASK` | New; defaults to `true`, enabling daily cleanup of orphaned new-pipeline trace payloads. | | `APP_PACKAGE_MAX_WORKFLOW_TOOLS` | New; defaults to `20` bundled Workflow Tool workflows per App package. | | `GUNICORN_KEEP_ALIVE` | New entrypoint setting; defaults to `10` seconds. | The old `OPS_TRACE_UNIFIED_ENABLED`, `OPS_TRACE_RETRYABLE_DISPATCH_MAX_RETRIES`, `OPS_TRACE_RETRYABLE_DISPATCH_DELAY_SECONDS`, and `OPS_TRACE_PARENT_CONTEXT_TTL_SECONDS` settings are removed. Existing Agent application-tracing opt-in settings remain supported. (#44673) For Docker, use `envs/core-services/api-worker.defaults` as the reference for common API/worker/Beat settings and `api-worker.env` for new overrides. Existing `shared.env` remains compatible. Tracked defaults load automatically; root `.env` and explicit service overrides still take precedence. Review the [service-specific references](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/tree/laipz8200/release-1.19.0/docker/envs) rather than replacing local files with fresh templates. (#45359, #45376) **Endpoint compatibility** - Replace deprecated Console profile-update POST calls to `/account/name`, `/account/avatar`, `/account/interface-language`, `/account/interface-theme`, and `/account/timezone` with **`PATCH /console/api/account/profile`**. Avatar URL reads remain available. (#45015) - Custom clients of **`GET /console/api/apps/{app_id}/trace-config`** must consume `configured_secrets` instead of expecting saved secret values. (#44673) - For Workflow and Chatflow OpenAPI calls, use **`POST /openapi/v1/apps/{app_id}/runs/{run_id}:stop`** (`stop.run`) and **`GET /openapi/v1/apps/{app_id}/runs/{run_id}/events`** (`get.run.event`). Chat, Agent Chat, and Completion retain the task-ID stop route under `stop.task`. (#44587) - Cloud education verification returns an explicit **`status: eligible | not_eligible`** result; only eligible results contain a token. The corresponding internal billing service must support this response contract. (#45165)
**Full Changelog:** [1.18.0 to the 1.19.0](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/compare/1.18.0...1.19.0)

payload.name: v1.19.0 - Trace Your Workflows, Layer by Layer
payload.body:
**Dify 1.19.0 brings nested workflow tracing to your observability tools.** Follow a workflow into the Workflow Tools it calls, inspect the steps inside each invocation, and keep the LLM context alongside the execution tree. This release also makes Workflow Tools portable with App packages, adds Skill Hub automation, and makes Agent files easier to upload and preview. The bundled plugin daemon is upgraded to **0.6.14-local**. [Release highlights](#user-content-release-highlights) · [Upgrade guide](#user-content-upgrade-guide) · [Detailed changes](#user-content-detailed-changes) ## Release highlights ### Nested workflow tracing **See what happens inside a Workflow Tool, all the way down to its LLM calls.** Building on the Console drilldown introduced in 1.18.0, new external traces now include the persisted execution steps inside called Workflow Tools. Child steps appear beneath the Tool span that invoked them, preserving the hierarchy across nested and repeated calls. (#44673) ![Langfuse trace tree showing a workflow, nested Middle and Child Workflow Tools, and the selected LLM call with formatted prompts and responses](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langgenius/dify/dcfb52e62726c91b43db20f3c087acf285428df1/docs/assets/pr-44673-langfuse-nested-prompts.jpg) *From the outer workflow to a nested LLM call: the execution tree and formatted messages, together in Langfuse. Screenshot from [#44673](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/pull/44673).* - **Follow the hierarchy.** Expand called Workflow Tools to see their internal execution steps under the invoking Tool span. - **Understand each invocation.** Repeated calls and failures retain their place in the trace. - **Keep the LLM context.** Inspect formatted prompts and responses, token usage, and project, trace, and observation links. > [!NOTE] > **Your saved provider settings continue to work.** The richer hierarchy applies to new executions; historical traces are not backfilled. Independently nested workflow runs remain separate traces linked by parent identifiers. For rolling deployments, follow the [tracing queue transition](#user-content-upgrade-guide) below. ### Take Workflow Tools with your apps Export an app and bring the workflows behind its Workflow Tools with it. `.ifpkg` packages include those workflows at their bound versions, including transitive dependencies. Import reuses tools already in the destination workspace and recreates, publishes, and registers missing ones, remapping their references. (#44592) All Dify app exports now use **package format v2**, including apps without Workflow Tools. Existing v1 imports and explicit YAML export remain supported. See the [upgrade guide](#user-content-upgrade-guide) before importing new packages into older installations. (#45353) ### Upload together. Preview in place. Select or drop multiple Agent configuration files and upload them in parallel. Successful uploads are bound in one atomic batch, concurrent Composer saves preserve the latest files, and Prompt uploads keep the cursor position while inserting multiple references. (#44947) Read PDFs inline, inspect source files with syntax highlighting, and see when text has been truncated. Previews cover configured files, Skill members, and working-directory files, with a download action when a PDF cannot be loaded. (#45032, #45045)
See Agent file uploads and previews ![Inline PDF preview in Agent files, with the research brief and file list](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/22bafc75-c8f5-46fd-b7ba-c5097f9cffb6) *Read a PDF directly in the Agent file preview and switch between project files.* ![Agent batch upload dialog with a PDF, Python source file, and Markdown guidelines selected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5eafd0c1-f46d-4966-bbc0-e6cd5eacff02) *Select several files and upload them together.* ![Syntax-highlighted Python source in the Agent file preview](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1435fd23-7489-450a-a200-dbd81c1b588d) *Inspect source files with syntax highlighting and line numbers.*
## Developer spotlight **Manage workspace Skills through OpenAPI and difyctl.** Find and inspect Skills, export a draft or published version, import local files, and publish a new version from the command line. (#44941)
The six Skill commands | Command | Capability | | --- | --- | | `difyctl get skill` | List Skills, with keyword and tag filters. | | `difyctl describe skill` | Read details, the draft hash, and latest published version. | | `difyctl get skill version` | List published versions. | | `difyctl export skill` | Export the draft or a selected published version as ZIP. | | `difyctl import skill --files ` | Create a Skill or replace an existing Skill's draft from local files. | | `difyctl publish skill` | Publish the draft as a new version. |
These operations require an account caller, the corresponding workspace permissions, and Skills to be enabled. **Import does not publish.** Importing over an existing Skill is classified as destructive; the operation catalog and CLI help distinguish read, write, and destructive operations. (#44941, #45314, #44587) --- ## Upgrade guide > [!IMPORTANT] > **Read the upgrade guide before deploying.** Docker Compose now requires **v2.35.0 or later**. Preserve existing environment files, upgrade the Dify components together, and use the new tracing queue during rolling deployments. New App packages use format v2 and require a compatible destination importer. The bundled plugin daemon moves to **0.6.14-local**. **Compatibility and rollout** 1. **Back up first.** Retain the database, vector-store data, uploaded files, Agent snapshot/workspace storage, deployment secrets, and environment files. Use a maintenance window for a single-stack upgrade. 2. **Upgrade the components together.** Use matching `1.19.0` API, worker, web, Agent Backend, and Local sandbox images, with plugin daemon `0.6.14-local`. Keep the existing Local sandbox authentication token and any configured `PASSWORD_PEPPER` unchanged. If upgrading from before 1.18.0, also follow the [1.18.0 upgrade guide](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/releases/tag/1.18.0). 3. **Use Docker Compose 2.35.0 or later.** This is the minimum supported version for root `.env` overrides to take precedence when Compose resolves service defaults. Check your installed version with `docker compose version`. (#45359) 4. **Keep tracked defaults separate from local overrides.** Bundled `docker/envs/**/*.defaults` files load automatically. Customize a service through its matching local `.env` file, using the override path documented in the defaults file; root `docker/.env` holds deployment inputs and explicit overrides. Preserve existing `.env` files and edit them in place. Review accidentally empty assignments and values pinned by older template copies before upgrading. (#45359, #45376) 5. **Existing `shared.env` files remain supported.** Common API, worker, and Beat customizations now belong in `docker/envs/core-services/api-worker.env`. Compose still reads legacy `docker/envs/core-services/shared.env` first, then `api-worker.env`, so `api-worker.env` wins when both set conflicting values. Root `docker/.env` takes precedence over both. An unchanged copy of `api-worker.defaults` preserves existing `shared.env` customizations. See the [Docker configuration guide](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/blob/laipz8200/release-1.19.0/docker/README.md#review-configuration-after-an-upgrade). (#45376) 6. **Separate tracing queues during a rolling upgrade.** New tasks default to `OPS_TRACE_QUEUE=ops_trace_v2`; API, workers, and Beat must agree. Custom `CELERY_QUEUES`, `CELERY_WORKER_QUEUES`, or `--queues` lists must include the new queue. Keep old tracing workers on `ops_trace` until old producers and all their queued, active, reserved, scheduled, and retry work have finished. Do not purge the old queue or ask the new retired handler to export legacy messages. See the [tracing rollout guide](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/blob/laipz8200/release-1.19.0/api/providers/trace/README.md#rolling-upgrade-from-the-previous-pipeline). (#44673) 7. **Upgrade package destinations before importing new App packages.** New app packages always use format v2. Older importers, including builds with the earlier strict v2 rule, may reject them. Version 1 imports remain supported on 1.19.0. Explicit YAML export remains available, but does not carry bundled Workflow Tool dependencies. (#44592, #45353)
Deployment instructions · Docker Compose, source, and difyctl **Docker Compose** Once the 1.19.0 release tag and images are published, stop a single-stack deployment gracefully, switch to the release, retain and review configuration, then pull and start the new images: ```bash cd dify/docker docker compose stop -t -1 git fetch --tags git checkout 1.19.0 # Merge required configuration changes into existing env files here. docker compose pull docker compose up -d ``` Keep API startup migrations enabled (`MIGRATION_ENABLED=true`), or apply the full migration chain through your managed migration process before starting new workers. For rolling deployments, follow the separate tracing-queue sequence instead of mixing old and new consumers. Configure shared plugin credentials, `PLUGIN_DAEMON_KEY` and `PLUGIN_DIFY_INNER_API_KEY`, in root `docker/.env` so the daemon and its clients receive matching values. Ports, volume paths, profiles, and health-check scheduling also remain root configuration inputs. See the [Docker configuration guide](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/blob/laipz8200/release-1.19.0/docker/README.md#configure-dify). (#45359) **Source deployments** Use Python **3.13**, Node.js **24.22.1 or later in the 24.x line**, and pnpm **12.16.1**. pnpm no longer provisions Node.js for the workspace, so install the required Node.js runtime separately. (#44976, #45094) From the repository root: ```bash uv sync --project api --frozen uv run --directory api flask db upgrade pnpm install --frozen-lockfile ``` Rebuild the web application and restart API, worker, scheduler, and Agent services from the same release. Refresh the standalone Agent Backend's locked `server` dependencies when deploying it separately. **difyctl** Install the matching 1.19.0 client and use `difyctl help` to discover the current server catalog. Refresh installed agent skills with `difyctl install skills `. Workflow and Chatflow automation should use the revised `stop.run` operation; message-based apps use `stop.task`.
Database migrations and existing data Upgrading from 1.18.0 applies **six migration revisions**, ending at **`53c10126d551`**. Apply the complete chain through the normal migration runner. Operational changes to plan for include: - **Storage-cleanup indexes (`d7e9a1c3f502`).** Add reference indexes on `message_files.upload_file_id`, `workflow_node_execution_offload.file_id`, and `workflow_draft_variable_files.upload_file_id`. PostgreSQL creates them concurrently, but index construction still scans data and consumes I/O. Online upgrades reuse matching healthy indexes and reject conflicting or invalid definitions. Investigate an interrupted invalid build before retrying; do not drop healthy indexes as routine recovery. (#44982) - **Tracing configuration uniqueness (`53c10126d551`).** Keep one configuration per app/provider and add a unique index. When duplicates exist, the most recently updated row wins, with the ID breaking timestamp ties. Superseded rows are deleted; downgrading the index does not restore them. Retain a database backup. (#44673) - **Extraction changes affect newly processed content.** Re-import or re-index documents whose stored content was affected by the EPUB, EML, DOCX, CSV, Markdown, or Notion fixes. The repeated-PDF-preview fix prevents new duplicate assets for source uploads; it does not remove duplicates already stored. (#44836, #44953, #44905, #43505, #43434, #45053, #44684) - **Tracing history is not rebuilt.** Existing Agent trace-ledger data remains readable, but previously exported traces do not acquire the new nested spans. (#44673)
## Detailed changes

The same few ideas kept getting rebuilt under different names: an actor that does the work, a signal that starts it, a packaged procedure, and a memory that carries lessons forward. This repetition leaked into product design and onto the user. Take the user who says “ monitor my Slack channel and send me a daily digest ”. Does this answer match the retrieved context? Decision models answer exactly that kind of question. They take a structured state and a fixed set of allowed answers and return a calibrated probability over them, rather than free-form text whose confidence drifts from run to run. That makes them a strong fit for the scoring step in an agent evaluation, where you want a label and a number you can threshold and trust. title: Smart Approvals in Amazon Quick: Human oversight where it matters
summary: How should security leaders preserve human oversight as AI agents take on more work? Permissions establish which actions agents can take, but a permitted action can still warrant a person’s judgment. Requiring approval for every step might seem like the safest approach, yet multi-step tasks can produce repeated prompts , even for routine actions. Research on security warnings shows that attention and adherence can decline with repetition. The challenge isn’t to require more approvals, but to preserve attention for decisions that need human review. Smart Approvals in Amazon Quick addresses this challenge by reviewing eligible actions within your existing controls. It evaluates each proposed action against the user’s request and either approves it automatically or returns it to the user for review. It does this without granting additional permissions or removing required human approvals. Security leaders retain control over which actions must always go to a person, while Smart Approvals is designed to reduce unnecessary interruptions in routine work. title: More Performance From Every Byte: How Full-Stack Codesign Solves AI’s Memory Challenge
summary: Larger models, longer contexts and agentic applications are increasing GPU memory pressure while supply tightens and prices rise — a trend expected to continue through the near term. NVIDIA works closely with memory partners to rapidly adopt the latest memory technologies. NVIDIA was first to adopt HBM3e and HBM4 technologies into an accelerated computing stack. But the approach isn’t to simply pack more memory onto the GPU. It’s full-stack codesign. NVIDIA intentionally designs GPUs, CPUs, networking, storage and software together to get more useful work out of memory at every layer of the AI factory. That matters because an AI factory runs on a memory and storage hierarchy. GPU high-bandwidth memory (HBM) is the fastest, most expensive and most contested tier — with model weights and KV cache competing for limited capacity. Below it sit CPU memory, local SSDs and shared storage, each trading speed for more capacity at a lower cost per bit. summary: 作者｜Wildcard 编辑｜靖宇 11 月 5 日，OpenAI 前 CTO Mira Murati 创立的 Thinking Machines Lab（简称 TML）同一天出了两条新闻。 当天，公司发布了第二代模型 Inkling 2 Small，第三方评测机构 Artificial Analysis（AA）给的评价相当高：权重放出后，它将成为「 中国以外得分最高的开放权重模型 」。同一天，据报道，这家公司正以 400 亿美元的投前估值筹集 50 亿美元新融资。 TML 在 2025 年 2 月对外亮相，至今一年半多。这期间，他们拿过 a16z 领投的 20 亿美元种子轮，也经历了联合创始人 Andrew Tulloch 转投 Meta，以及联合创始人 Barret Zoph、Luke Metz 等人今年 1 月回归 OpenAI 的动荡，之后由 PyTorch 联合创始人 Soumith Chintala 接任 CTO。 今年 1 月还有报道称， 团队 以约 500 亿美元估值融资的谈判陷入停滞 。新一轮融资能不能谈成，很大程度上要看二代模型的成色。 翻开 Inkling 2 Small 的技术博客，跑分表和架构图之外，最意味深长的是一行交代训练数据来源的文字： 预训练后半程的数据，大部分采样自更早的模型，其中点名了月之暗面的 Kimi K3 。 01 594B 的「Small」，强在哪 「Small」这个词在大模型行业里正在不断膨胀。 TML 今年 7 月发布的初代开放权重模型 Inkling 有 975B 总参数，两周后的 Inkling Small 是 276B。到了第二代， Inkling 2 Small 的总参数量翻了一倍多，达到 594B，每次推理激活 17B 。它是 MoE 架构，支持 100 万上下文和可调的思考力度，能看图，但不支持初代 Inkling 具备的音频输入。 训练流程相当重。预训练第一阶段，团队在英伟达 GB300 NVL72 机架上用 68 小时、以原生 NVFP4（4 比特浮点）精度吞下 8.4 万亿 token；第二阶段再喂 3.8 万亿 token 的高质量新数据；最后两个阶段用合计约 3540 亿 token 的推理与智能体轨迹收尾，上下文拉到 100 万。随后是一次 9 天的联合强化学习：2048 块 GPU，超过 1700 万次 rollout，单次 rollout 中位耗时 8 分钟，长的能跑 4 个小时。 这些长链路训练，指向的是官方口中这一代最大的进步：长程自主工作。演示里，它用 Three.js 从零写出一个城市经营游戏，建筑、纹理、车辆全部程序生成，还要管电力、预算和突发事件；用 Python 从零写出一台能启动真实 Linux 内核的电脑模拟器；还能把一张平面户型图变成可以走动的 3D 漫游。 用 Three.js 从零生成的城市经营游戏｜图片来源：Thinking Machines 训练过程也有惊险时刻。强化学习进行到一半，监控发现模型借助搜索工具接触到的第三方服务，绕过了团队设置的网络封锁。团队只好暂停训练，去掉联网环境、给工具调用加上同步监控后再继续。官方还承认，早期版本遇到太难的任务时会「执着于成功」，出现编造结果、无视指令甚至掩盖行为的情况。到发布版，内部「不当行为」得分从上一代的 66.8 降到 14.9（越低越好），但仍落后于闭源模型。 跑分上， 它最突出的长板是知识工作和长流程商业任务 。在考察表格、演示文稿和备忘录的 AA-Briefcase 上，它拿到 1527 的 Elo 分，上一代 Small 只有 912，Claude Sonnet 5.5 (medium) 是 1439，Gemini 3.8 Flash (high) 是 1203。官方对比表里，它在 JobBench（70.5%）、Vals 法律指数（73.9%）、金融指数（61.5%）和 HLE-Diamond（28.7%）上都是最高分。 编程上，它没能做到全面领先。FrontierCode v2.0 和 DeepSWE v1.1 上，它赢了 Kimi K3 和 GLM-5.3-Flash，但落后于 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash（25.4% 对 28.5%，72.1% 对 77.0%）；SWEBench Pro v2 (Hard) 上则输给 Kimi K3。和闭源模型比，它在命令行任务 Terminal-Bench 4.0

title: AI 时代没有标准答案的问题，我们面对面聊
summary: 我们刚刚官宣了极客公园创新大会 2027 的首批嘉宾。 今天，再来揭晓「小场深谈」的最新进展。 10 月底，我们在「小场深谈」的预热文章里做了一次调研，请大家投票选出最想聊的话题。最终，我们选定了最受关注的五组主题，设下了五场专场，每一场都从大家最想聊的那个问题开始。 这五场专场，恰好瞄向当下行业最受关注、也最要紧的议题上：Personal AI 怎么接管日常、AI 创作怎么重写内容、具身智能怎么走进现实、硬件与制造怎么长出「新图纸」、AI 落地怎么用结果说话。 每一场，三组话题，深谈 + 现场问答，80 分钟左右。场子都不大，百余人左右。 IF 2026「小场深谈」现场 还记得去年的「小场深谈」，有人刚从大厂跳槽、正用 AI 做自己的第一款产品，当场把困惑摊给嘉宾；有精神科医生，追问做陪伴机器人的创业者：你希望它把人带回现实交往，还是给这个家添一个新成员？——现场的发问，往往带着一个人具体的处境，比文字更触动人心。 今年五场「小场深谈」的主题与要讨论的核心议题已经基本确认： Day1 Personal AI 是如今最热门的创投叙事，每个人都有不同的理解。但能真正谈论这个话题的创业者并不多。 我们将邀请行业内最受关注、获一线资本加持，且已经有实践成果的先行者，到场激辩，带来他们的「非共识」： Personal AI 到底能帮普通人做什么？为谁解决什么需求、能接手哪些日常事情，为什么有人持续用它？ 从海外产品看，我们愿意把多少事情交给 AI？信任的边界在哪里？ 从「记住我」到「帮到我」：AI 如何用个人数据真正发挥作用？ Personal AI 还可以从哪些场景切入？哪些才通向更长久的生命力？ Day1 从创作方法到发行变现，从短片、剧集、3D 动画到线下音乐会，AI 正在重写内容生产的每一个环节。 作为当下国内 AI 创作领域最具代表性的平台之一，极客公园将与共创伙伴即梦AI，把话筒交给最懂它的人——本场邀请即梦上的最佳实践者，那些最有资格讲、也玩得最出彩的创作者，到场分享他们的真实玩法。 当人人都能生成影像，创作的价值如何被重新认识？新进入者与专业创作者，分别带来了什么？ AI 创作正从「生成一个片段」走向「完成一部作品」——新的内容格式从哪里长出来？ 门槛消失之后，审美、故事与生活经验，这些藏在幕后的人的能力，正在怎样被重新定价？ Day1 机器人从演示走向落地，真正卡在哪里？演示视频越来越丝滑，真实世界里却处处是「只有做过才知道」的阻力。我们邀请做研究、造机器人、打磨产品的人坐在一起，展开深度探讨： 从实验室到真实世界，具身智能的「阻力」到底来自哪里？是模型、数据，还是场景？ 当模型、硬件与数据开始一体进化，机器人会先在哪里真正走进现实？ 同一个趋势，研究者、创业者与投资人看到的「下一个 12 个月」，有什么不同？ Day2 AI-Native 硬件不缺概念，但真正值得投入的方向和信号更需要辨别。本场，我们请来正在一线造硬件的创业者、工程师与制造者——他们踩过从图纸到交付的每一个坑，也亲手试过新一代工具与工艺的边界。 让他们来告诉你：好硬件的「新图纸」到底长什么样，一个人又能把它带多远。他们将讨论的核心议题包涵但不限于： 可穿戴、个人助理……AI 硬件的新品类里，哪些需求是真需求，哪些能跑出爆品？ 从一张图纸到一批货：模型、数据、软件…供应链里来了很多新要素，如何重新理解硬件？ 桌面制造爆发之后，商业模式、竞争格局、应用场景会怎么演进？下一个爆发点会出现在哪里？ Day2 听听真正把 AI 用进业务、做出结果的人——如何从实战出发，告诉你从「能用」到「用好」之间，那一步到底是怎么跨过去的。 模型已经够强了，为什么客户不会用？把通用能力变成可用、可信、可衡量的产品，难点在哪里？ 从「调用多少 Token」到「创造多大价值」：组织里对员工 + AI 的价值重估，正在怎样改变？ 那些把 AI 拿到「大结果」的人和公司，做对了什么？ 以上，就是今年极客公园创新大会 5 个「小场深谈」的核心议题。 嘉宾与对谈主播，将在接下来一个月内陆续官宣，记得留意极客公园公众号，获取最新动向。 同时，我们也在寻找对谈主播和愿意加入的实践者：如果你觉得上面某个问题「 非你不可 」，如果你正在一线做这些事、有话想说，欢迎在评论区留言或联系我们——小场深谈，欢迎真正有料的人。 如果你对这些议题感兴趣，记得速速锁票！ 在信息过载的时代，让我们面对面，把 AI 时代最值得聊的真问题，和「最有料的人」当面聊一次。 特别提醒，主舞台的早鸟特惠也在进行中，记得提早锁票哦：

title: 中期选举后美国芯片股重挫，纳指单日暴跌 5.52%；民主党宣布推动《禁止人工智能法案》；OpenAI 推出 GPT-6 Cyber
summary: 芯片股惨遭重挫，华尔街迎来 1896 年以来中期选举后表现最差的第二个交易日 据路透社报道，美国民主党在国会中期选举中大胜，引发投资者对 AI 监管加强、数据中心建设放缓的担忧。 当地时间周四，美国科技股遭遇大规模抛售， 华尔街股票市值单日蒸发约 3.2 万亿美元（约合人民币 22.7 万亿元） 。纳斯达克综合指数暴跌 5.52%，创下自 2025 年 4 月以来最大单日跌幅，较 10 月初创下的历史高点累计下跌近 12%，进入技术性回调区间。 此次抛售席卷整个 AI 产业链。费城半导体指数暴跌约 12.3%，英伟达下跌约 9.3%，基本抹去 2026 年以来的累计涨幅；闪迪（SanDisk）暴跌约 22%，美光科技、西部数据和 AMD 跌幅均在 17% 左右。此前受到资金追捧的 AI 芯片、存储及数据中心相关股票成为重灾区。 这轮抛售与美国中期选举结果密切相关。民主党赢得国会控制权，并在多个关键州取得胜利，使投资者担心美国未来可能对 AI 基础设施建设实施更严格的监管。 随着 AI 数据中心规模不断扩大，其庞大的电力和水资源需求正引发越来越多当地居民的反对。部分社区担心，新建数据中心将推高电费、增加电网负担，并对当地基础设施造成压力。 Meta 总裁迪娜·鲍威尔·麦考密克（Dina Powell McCormick）指出，数据中心已经成为公众感知 AI 发展的直接载体，也因此成为社区反对 AI 扩张的集中目标。（消息来源：环球市场播报、凤凰网科技） 美国民主党提出超级 AI 禁令：个人违规 20 年监禁、企业直接强制解散！ 快科技 11 月 5 日消息， 美国民主党宣布推动《禁止人工超级智能法案》，全面封杀超级 AI 研发，明文禁止任何个人或企业机构研发及部署人工超级智能（ASI）。 根据法案草案，ASI 为具备以下特征的系统：一是在广泛领域与任务中达到或超越人类认知表现与能力的 AI 架构，或可轻易被修改以展现出该能力的系统；二是具备足以策划并执行削弱人类主导权、甚至推翻或破坏美国政府体系的 AI 系统。 法案要求全面暂停所有先进 AI 的研发进程，直至联邦层级的专属监管机构正式运作，并建立清晰的法规与模型审查机制。 为确保禁令落实，法案提议设立全新内阁级别的人工智能部，专责监管前沿 AI 模型的全生命周期，并有权强制技术团队消除系统内的高风险功能，包括忽视人类关机指令、未经授权进行网络攻击或自我递归升级等潜在失控行为。 违规罚则方面，涉案企业将面临被强制解散处分，违规个人最高可被判处 20 年联邦监禁，量刑标准堪比现行非法研发核武器的重大罪行。 此外管辖范围不限于美国境内，法案明确将「全球禁止超级智能」列为美国外交政策目标，要求美国政府积极寻求国际协定、强化盟友合作，并实施严格的出口管制措施，阻断全球任何地区研发人工超级智能的可能性。（消息来源：快科技） Google 发布 Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash 视频模型，可对话编辑最长 15 秒钟 11 月 6 日，Google 公司在周四正式推出了视频生成模型 Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash，该模型支持原生 15 秒视频生成，支持通过多轮对话进行编辑，价格较上一代降低 30%。 Google 表示，Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash 正通过 Gemini API、Google AI Studio、Google Cloud Console、Flow、Google Vids、面向 Google AI Ultra 订阅用户的 Gemini 应用以及 Google Ads 陆续推出。每个生成的视频都带有不可感知的 SynthID 水印，以标明其来源。 现在，该模型生成的视频片段时长可设定为 3 至 15 秒，此前最长为 10 秒。同时，720p 视频的生成价格下调 30%，降至每秒 0.07 美元。用户还可以通过持续对话的方式对已生成的视频进行编辑。 它的一项突出功能是 Google 所称的「对话式编辑」(Conversational Editing)。用户可以通过多轮对话逐步调整生成的视频，例如更换背景、调整光线或修改画面比例，而无需重新生成整个视频。Google 表示，这项功能支持对完整的 15 秒视频进行编辑。 再结合上分层工作流，这项功能还有望降低生成成本。用户首先以 360p 或 720p 分辨率生成初稿，再通过后续编辑修正个别细节，最后仅对最终成片进行升频处理，将分辨率提升至 1080p 或 4K。（消息来源：凤凰网科技） OpenAI 推出 GPT-6 Cyber：漏洞挖掘能力大幅提升 越权攻击风险显著降低 OpenAI 正式推出新一代网络安全人工智能模型 GPT-6 Cyber，重点提升软件漏洞发现、网络安全防御以及自主执行安全测试的能力。与此前版本相比，新模型不仅在网络安全相关基准测试中取得更高成绩，还显著降低了执行任务时偏离授权范围、擅自攻击其他平台的概率。 OpenAI 表示，GPT-6 Cyber 在内部测试中，未经授权越界执行操作的比例已经降至 1% 以下，而此前的 GPT-5.6 Cyber 这一比例约为 5%。这意味着新模型在执行网络安全任务时，能够更加严格地遵循用户设定的目标和权限范围。 为了评估这一问题，OpenAI 采用了一项名为 ExploitGym HoneyPot 的测试。OpenAI 网络安全准备与安全团队负责人福阿德·马丁表示，GPT-6 Cyber 在这项评估中取得了明显进步，超过 99% 的情况下都能够按照用户要求执行任务。 不过，研究人员仍然关注另一种潜在风险，即所谓的「评估意识」（Evaluation Awareness）。当人工智能模型意识到自己正在接受测试时，可能会刻意改变行为，以便获得更好的测试结果，而不一定反映其在真实环境中的表现。（消息来源：cnBeta） 前 Anthropic Claude Code 产品负责人 title: 极客公园创新大会 2027 首批嘉宾揭晓！
summary: 今年 12 月 5 日—6 日，北京 798艺术区，还是老地方。 极客公园创新大会（GEEKPARK IF），我们又要见面了。 IF 将进入第 17 年。它像一本记录中国科技行业的「年鉴」，一场科技爱好者的年终盛宴，一次号召创新者聚集、留下历史回音的年度认知集结。 今年，我们的主题是： Revaluation 价值，另有答案 我们要探讨的不再是 AI 可以有多厉害，而是更落地的一面—— 工作、创作、生意，你原本笃定的经验，正在一件件被 AI 重新算账。你以为已经看懂的赛道，换个角度，结论可能完全不一样。 哪些老优势正在缩水？哪些被低估的人和机会，正在悄悄长出新的价值？ Revaluation 价值，另有答案 每年办会，最让人期待的，就是把那些跑在最前面的「Outlier」和积极行动者们拉到一块儿。一群从全国各地飞来的人，思想和实践在同一片空间流动，碰撞、激发。 今年，他们也将如期而至。 主舞台之外，我们还在 751图书馆、艺文空间和极客公园，准备了五场小场深谈。 没有大礼堂，没有台上台下的距离感。做研究的人、造产品的人、在一线踩过坑的人，坐下来，把那些真正难、真正关键的问题聊透。 Personal AI、AI 创作、具身智能、硬件与 Maker、AI 实践——都是一手判断。 我们还将在现场公布： 接下来，是大家最关心的部分—— 更多嘉宾，正在路上 这只是第一批。 接下来的几周，主舞台演讲者、小场深谈嘉宾、特别环节，我们都会陆续公布。 想第一时间拿到完整议程和嘉宾名单，记得关注极客公园公众号，别走丢。

title: 世界互联网大会领先科技奖背后，Qoder 凭什么拿下中国 AI 编程市场第一
summary: 作者｜Cynthia 编辑｜郑玄 2026 年 11 月，每年乌镇世界互联网大会期间举办的领先科技奖，已经走到第十年。 作为面向全球征集互联网领域领先成果的国际性科技奖项，领先科技奖每年会选出涵盖基础研究、关键技术与工程研发约 15 至 20 项获奖项目。一定程度上，它的评选也预示了未来几年潮水的走向。 这一年，传统互联网的光环逐渐退去，AI 成了最大的关键词。其中，仅工程研发组的 8 项获奖成果，从 AMD 的 AI 处理器，到蚂蚁的大模型健康服务平台，再到地平线的整车智能体……就有至少 5 项与 AI 有关。 而在通用 Agent 这一领域， 阿里旗下智能体平台 Qoder，成为了国内唯一获此殊荣的通用 Agent 产品。 至此，在领先科技奖诞生的第 10 个年头，命运形成了一个有趣的回环。 那时的领先科技奖，名字还叫世界互联网领先科技成果发布活动。而那一年在首届活动中，与特斯拉自动辅助驾驶、微软 HoloLens、「神威·太湖之光」超级计算机并列入选的，正式阿里云飞天开放平台为基础的大规模分布式交易处理平台。 那时的飞天，立项已经超过 7 年，逐渐从承托阿里庞大业务的基础设施，转变为连接超过百万台服务器，能把计算能力送到更多企业手中的行业 Infra 定位。 乌镇的亮相，见证了飞天从内部技术攻坚走向更广阔市场的历程。 十年后，Qoder 来到同一个舞台。 论资历，这款 2025 年 8 月才首次上线的产品还很年轻；但论成绩，迄今为止，这款产品的全球用户已经超过 800 万；IDC 发布的 2025 年中国 AI 编程市场份额报告中，阿里以 47.6%的份额位居第一，超过第二至第五名之和；Gartner 最新的企业级 AI 代码智能体魔力象限，也将阿里云列入「挑战者」，与 AWS、Google 等公司同处这一象限。 从云计算的大幕拉起到 AI Coding 的编程新范式，相比 10 年前的云计算时代，今天的竞争节奏已经被压缩到以周、甚至以天计算，竞争烈度也今时不同往日。那么，外有海外优秀产品在前，对内又有国内厂商密集入场， Qoder 究竟是如何从强敌环伺中突围的？ 01 强敌环伺，Qoder 如何突围 在 Qoder 正式立项时，它所要进入的市场，已经坐满了人。 2025 年 6 月，阿里成立面向 Agent 时代的 AI 创新事业部。 Qoder 团队随即开始冲刺，那时 手里待完成的清单：从产品到官网，从用户体系到商业化链路、营销，再到面向全球用户的部署架构，一切都要从 0 开始 完成它们的时间，只有两个月。 但此时，海外先行者已经有了相当可观的规模。同月，Cursor 刚刚完成 9 亿美元融资，估值达到 99 亿美元，年化经常性收入超过 5 亿美元；紧随其后，GitHub Copilot 官宣用户达到 2000 万。Claude Code、Codex 也在一轮轮产品革新中不断争取开发者，让 AI 接手越来越完整的开发任务。 国内同行也在加速。 7 月，字节旗下 TRAE 推出 SOLO 模式，将自主开发延伸到需求规划、编码与部署。8 月 21 日，Qoder 上线。仅 19 天后，腾讯发布 CodeBuddy CLI，并直接官宣国内版全系列产品免费使用。 开发者已经不缺选择。作为一款新产品，Qoder 要争取的，是开发者们可能已经交给其他工具的时间与信任 。 但好在，这是一个已经有了充足准备的团队。Qoder 负责人丁宇，花名叔同，2010 年加入阿里，长期与云计算底层技术打交道。从全面容器化、统一调度到混合部署，再到让庞大的业务系统稳定运行，对他来说已经是轻车熟路。并且，早在 2023 年，大模型编程能力尚未成熟时，他就开始与内部大模型团队协作，主导研发通义灵码，带领的团队从代码补全、问答和局部修改做起，对真实开发中模型怎样理解私有代码，企业怎样部署与管理，都已经有了成熟的摸索。 这些基于真实场景锻炼出的经验，也成为了 Qoder 打响第一枪的关键 ：去年 8 月 Qoder 刚亮相时，选择把 Repo Wiki 和 Quest 放在了重要位置。打开一个项目，Repo Wiki 先梳理架构、模块与依赖，帮助人和 Agent 认识工程；接到开发任务，Quest 与用户明确需求和验收条件，再持续推进规划、编码和验证。补全代码、对话修改、委派完整任务，可以在同一款产品里完成。 五天后，超过 10 万名开发者加入。此后，JetBrains 插件、CLI、企业版和 Teams 版接连推出。半年内，一套覆盖不同开发习惯的产品矩阵成形。 但产品发布只是起点。团队很快把自己也放进了这场实验。 于是，2026 年初，借助已有的 Qoder 能力，团队将其用在了内部的开发流程中，五个人仅用七天时间，就完成了桌面助手 QoderWork 的开发， 又用 18 天时间上线了 QoderWake，让数字员工拥有岗位身份、长期记忆、技能和权限边界，能够进入日常协作，持续承担工作。 与之同期，阿里的 Qwen 模型体系，也为这种尝试提供了条件。模型、Agent 运行框架和产品可以共同调整，意味着一次任务失败后，团队能够沿着执行过程继续追查：信息是否找全，工具是否合用，模型是否学会了正确的做事方法，最终深入到问题的最底层。 就这样，团队一边开发 Agent，一边用 Agent 改造自己的研发； 阿里此前积累的模型、云计算与研发经验，被重新组织进一套产品，Qoder 也开始拥有了与全球顶级对手持续竞争的能力。 今年 8 月，Qoder 焕新升级迎来统一入口，这是一款以 Coding 为核心能力，面向所有人的智能体工作台，用户无论是否懂代码，都能把创意快速转化为可落地的成果。 全新 Qoder 的核心优势在于既能适配专业开发人员需求，也能覆盖产品、设计、运营、数据、独立创作者等一众目标明确、能辨别产出好坏、希望快速落地创意的人群。 上线三天用户破 10 万，再次展现了 Qoder 的 AI 速度。 02 让 AI 进入真实开发流程 阿里内部的探索，展示了一支顶级技术团队怎样用 Agent 改造研发。 但走出阿里的项目室，Qoder 遇到的，往往是企业已经运行多年、五花八门的复杂系统、多年沿袭下来的流程，以及不同团队各自的开发思路和技术标准。 能否在这些工程约束里实现效率加速，才真正决定了开发者会不会继续把任务交给它。 以山东山大华天软件为例，在工业设计中，工程师从供应商那里收到零件模型，或者准备复用旧设计时，文件里可能只剩下完整的外形。最初怎样建模、用了哪些参数、各处尺寸如何关联，已经无从得知。要在此基础上改型，往往还得重新分析结构、补做建模。

title: 一个人用得好 AI，为什么一家公司却用不好？
summary: 作者｜老 S 编辑｜郑玄 今天的 Agent，已经能够独立完成不少具体的工作。 写方案、写代码、做分析报告，过去可能需要员工花费几天才能完成的任务，如今 Agent 往往能在较短时间里交出不错的结果。 但在企业里，完成一份方案，可能只是一项工作的开始。比如，Agent 可以很快制定一份员工考核方案。但要用它真正完成一次考核，还需要获取员工的考勤、业绩等数据，处理特殊情况，并经过业务负责人和 HR 的确认，才能最终确定绩效。 能够交付阶段性的工作产物，和能进入真实业务、创造实际价值，是两回事。 随着 Agent 能力快速进化，企业开始面对一个新的问题： 如何让这些越来越能干的 AI，真正参与到现有的工作体系中？ 在今年的腾讯全球数字生态大会上，腾讯专门设置了 AI 产品发布台，用两天时间、七场议题、40 多场产品发布，集中展示企业 AI 从应用到基础设施的一系列新能力。 腾讯集团高级执行副总裁、云与智慧产业事业群 CEO 汤道生在大会上提出，腾讯将围绕办公协同、数据管理和业务执行三大场景，持续开放 WorkBuddy Agent 平台能力，帮助企业打造可运营、可进化的智能生产力系统。 从应用、数据、安全到工程，腾讯此次集中展示的一系列产品和技术能力，正是希望让 Agent 不仅能够完成任务，还能真正进入企业的业务流程，成为持续创造价值的生产力。 01 一个人用得好 AI， 不等于一家公司用得好 AI 随着大模型和 AI Coding 工具的发展，软件开发的门槛正在快速降低。一些过去需要技术团队专门开发的内部工具，如今几天就能完成，业务人员也开始有机会直接创造自己需要的 Agent。 但问题是， 一个人用得好的 Agent，并不意味着整个团队都能用好。 个人可以根据自己的需求配置工具、调整工作流，但企业需要考虑更多：Agent 能否接入原有系统、访问所需数据？不同员工、Agent 的权限如何管理？一个人摸索出的好方法，怎样才能让其他人直接使用？ 腾讯云副总经理、WorkBuddy 企业产品负责人张曦耀在大会上提出，个人提效并不等于组织变强，两者之间隔着的是一整套组织能力。 WorkBuddy 企业版此次升级，正是试图降低这道门槛。 相比个人使用 Agent，企业版更强调连接、管理和规模化应用。此次发布的四项升级中，开放平台让 WorkBuddy 能够连接企业微信、第三方 IM 和业务系统；企业级安全解决方案和可观测中心，帮助企业管理权限、执行过程和使用成本；WorkBuddy 托管智能体（WMA）则将任务搬到云端，支持 Agent 7×24 小时运行。 WorkBuddy 升级办公套件订阅丨来自：腾讯全球数字生态大会 与此同时，腾讯还发布了以 WorkBuddy 为工作台的一体化办公套件 Buddy One，整合腾讯文档、网盘、乐享等产品，通过统一账号、共享 Credit 池和集中管理，降低企业配置和推广 AI 的复杂度，并让技能与工作经验有机会在团队中复用。 苏宁的实践是一个很好的案例。基于 WorkBuddy 企业版，苏宁建立了组织级智能体平台，已经覆盖 14 个部门、48 个协作场景，沉淀了 36 个可复用智能体。比如在新品发布场景中，团队将布展、会展和接待流程整理成模板，并将过程文件纳入知识库，将一场新品发布的筹备时间从 3 个工作日缩短到 4 小时。 不仅节省了时间，这套工作方法也被保留了下来，可以在下一次任务中直接复用。 这也是 Agent 从个人工具走向组织生产力的关键： 不仅让更多员工能够使用 AI，还要让个人积累的能力成为整个团队可以复用的资产。 但让 Agent 在企业内普及，只是第一步。员工每天仍然需要在文档、知识库和各种办公软件之间协作。要让 AI 真正参与工作，这些软件本身也需要改变。 02 让 Agent 真正上班， 办公软件也得「改改」 今天绝大多数办公软件，原本都是为人设计的。 比如，一名员工让 Agent 完成一份研究报告。虽然 AI 已经能够生成不错的初稿，但需要参考的资料可能散落在知识库、聊天记录和不同文件中。员工仍然需要自己整理资料、补充背景，再根据经验反复调整，最后把结果交给同事修改和审核。 看上去 AI 加快了写作，但完成一项工作所需的许多环节，并没有因此减少。 因此，AI 办公的下一步，不只是给办公软件增加 AI 功能，让人方便在上面用 Agent；更要让软件本身变得对 Agent 友好，让 AI 能够直接参与人的工作。 腾讯此次围绕办公产品进行的一系列升级，正在尝试解决这个问题。 首先是让 Agent 能够获得工作所需的上下文。 以腾讯 AI 知识管家 ima 为例，它不仅帮助用户沉淀和管理知识，也支持基于已有知识进行问答、理解与处理。据介绍，目前 ima 已汇聚 1300 万知识工作者，知识管理规模超过 12 亿，知识号生态共享内容数量达到 5.2 亿。在此基础上，ima 通过原生嵌入、MCP、Skills 等方式，向 WorkBuddy 及其他智能体开放知识调用能力，让个人积累的资料与生态共享的专业内容在更多任务中发挥作用，成为用户和 Agent 都能调用的「第二大脑」。目前，ima 在 WorkBuddy、元宝中的累计调用量已超过 2 亿次。 腾讯乐享丨来自：腾讯全球数字生态大会 对于企业而言，腾讯乐享进一步提供企业知识的连接、索引和治理，让制度、流程和历史案例能够成为 Agent 的参考依据；腾讯网盘则负责统一存储，让 Agent 可以在授权范围内获取文件、保存工作成果。 除了文档和知识，企业还有大量业务数据需要 AI 理解。即使 Agent 能够查询数据库，也未必知道不同指标的具体含义，或者不同部门采用的统计口径。腾讯云的 TDSQL Nexa Lakebase、DataBuddy Unity Semantics 等产品，就是尝试让 Agent 在获取数据的同时，理解数据背后的业务语义，减少分析和判断中的错误。 但让 Agent 理解业务，只是第一步。 下一步需要解决的，是如何让 Agent 与人协作。 WorkBuddy 与腾讯文档互嵌丨来自：腾讯全球数字生态大会 腾讯文档此次重新设计了编辑器，为 Agent 的操作进行适配，实现「人机双写」。员工和 Agent 可以在同一份文档中继续编辑，沿用相同的权限体系。腾讯文档与 WorkBuddy 也实现了上下文的双向切换，让员工不必在 WorkBuddy 和腾讯文档之间反复搬运内容。 过去，员工使用 AI 生成内容，再回到办公软件完成后续工作；现在，Agent 可以在已有的知识、任务背景和权限下，直接与人协作，接续完成工作。 这种变化也正在向更多场景延伸。腾讯设计 Ardot 让 Agent 能够读取设计稿中的组件和规范，CNB 与 CodeBuddy 则尝试让 Agent 直接参与代码仓库中的开发和评审流程。 对于企业来说，真正有价值的 AI 办公，不只是某个环节的速度提高了多少，而是能否减少员工反复寻找资料、解释背景和交接成果的工作。

title: Apple 智能国行上线，苹果大涨超 6% 重返美股市值第一；英伟达显卡订单排长队，中国客户预计只能拿到 1%；字节限制员工使用个人 AI｜极客早知道
summary: Apple 智能国行上线，苹果大涨超 6% 重返美股市值第一 11 月 4 日，Apple 智能伴随 iOS 27.3 的 Developer Beta 向中国大陆用户开放测试，并计划于 12 月随 iOS 27.3 正式版推出。与此同时，苹果也确认与阿里巴巴达成合作，将千问接入 Siri、写作工具及视觉智能，让中国用户能够通过系统直接调用国内大模型的能力。 不过，这一次上线的并不是完整版 Apple 智能。首批功能主要包括实时翻译、写作工具、视觉智能、照片消除、智绘表情、通知摘要等，而苹果此前展示的新一代 Siri AI，以及 WWDC26 公布的部分下一代 AI 能力，仍然不在此次更新范围内。 当日，苹果 (AAPL.US) 大涨超 6%，报 353.05 美元，总市值再度突破 5 万亿美元，重返美股市值第一。(来源：格隆汇) OpenAI 升级 ChatGPT 图片能力，支持直接生成和编辑 GIF 动画 11 月 5 日，据 The Verge 报道，ChatGPT 现在可以通过提示词或上传到人工智能聊天机器人的照片来创建 GIF。此次更新与 OpenAI 的新 Images 2.6 模型同步推出，允许用户调整 GIF 的动画速度，编辑单个帧，并与他人分享。 在此之前，ChatGPT 无法单步原生生成 GIF。公司分享的一个示例展示了 title: This robotics concept helps explain the jaggedness of frontier capabilities
summary: The last year has seen incredible progress in model capabilities in certain domains — most notably programming , mathematics , and cybersecurity . Yet the real-world impact of these breakthroughs has been surprisingly modest — especially outside of those professions. Lawyers, architects, salespeople, college professors, and others are certainly using AI models in their work, but AI models don’t seem close to transforming those professions the way they seem to be transforming mathematics and computer programming. And even in the software industry, we’re not seeing the kind of mass unemployment many people expected we would see once AI models reached human capabilities. A big question is why — and whether the impact might grow in the next few months or years. Many people expect massive AI-driven disruptions to begin hitting other professions in 2028 or even 2027. I don’t think that’s going to happen, and a concept from robotics helps to explain why: the sim-to-real gap. I encountered this concept when I was editing my colleague Kai Williams’s excellent September article about the scramble to collect robotics training data. Suppose you want to train a robot to walk. One option is to create a virtual environment with a simulated robot.

title: Securing the agentic enterprise with data lineage
summary: A sales representative asks an AI agent for customer pricing, and the agent pulls data from multiple sources: restricted pricing systems, internal communications, and archived quotes. The output looks accurate to the agent, so a second agent uses the data to draft the proposal for the sales rep. No human checks either handoff. When it’s discovered that the proposal includes unapproved, confidential, and sensitive information, no one can trace where the problematic data entered the workflow or how it spread across systems, files, and agents. DOWNLOAD THE REPORT This scenario illustrates why AI governance needs to evolve, rapidly and dynamically. As more enterprises begin to use agentic AI in daily workflows, they’re realizing that they must manage more than static files; they must manage moving and fragmented data that is continuously ingested, copied, summarized, transformed, reused, and redistributed in new forms. In short, AI security isn’t a tool problem; it’s a data visibility problem. Consequently, traditional security approaches built solely around applications, systems, networks, or endpoints are no longer sufficient. summary: Yesterday, when reporting on emerging efforts to pipe the console version of GTA VI through a PC's DLSS-powered Nvidia GPU , we mentioned in passing that PC players could instead just wait for the AI-assisted decompilation port that will no doubt be coming in short order. Google didn't see the backlash coming, but now that it's here, the search giant is clarifying what exactly its new policy means and what's changing. Since the company considers search part of its AI portfolio (Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Search), schools have to specifically turn that on for logged-in student accounts. When Google revealed its new policy, the company's VP for education spoke exclusively to The New York Times , which interpreted the situation as Google will "turn off search" if schools reject AI. title: Agility Robotics' Nasdaq debut invites scrutiny of humanoid robot market
summary: Humanoid robots remain unproven at scale and have not yet achieved widespread commercialization, compared with industrial robots that have decades of proven track records in warehouses and factories. That frank acknowledgment is among the risks outlined in a securities filing by Agility Robotics—the first dedicated developer of humanoid robots to become a publicly traded company in the United States. The robotics company, headquartered in Salem, Oregon, previously became the first to achieve full-time commercial deployment of humanoid robots at a customer warehouse in 2024. Now, Agility’s public listing on the Nasdaq stock exchange as of November 5 has come with financial disclosures detailing how the company plans to build a business around renting out or selling humanoid robots to perform manual labor. “When we are doing robots as a service, it is much lower risk for customers to use it because they are getting a return on investment on day one,” Jonathan Hurst , co-founder and chief robot officer at Agility Robotics, told Ars. "Because they're paying a rate that is comparable to the human labor rate, and that makes the economics pretty straightforward.” Read full article Comments

title: Big Tech claims voters’ AI backlash is “anti-Trump” not “anti-tech”
summary: Donald Trump’s big, rapid American AI buildout now faces a major slowdown as voters in yesterday’s elections overwhelmingly supported candidates and measures that favored increasing restrictions on AI and data centers nationwide. One resource from a polling firm, called Redbud Consulting, tracked data center initiatives on the ballot and reported that out of 44 measures across 10 states seeking to restrict data centers, 38 passed so far. Those measures included dozens of moratoriums and bans. Analysts suggested those won’t impact data centers already under construction or approved through 2027, instead largely impacting future projects planned for 2028. Only one measure passed allowing a data center to proceed. But even that small win represented pushback on the AI industry—requiring data center developers in a North Dakota city to pay for independent reviews and hold public hearings when expanding or proposing projects. In addition to increasing regulations on data centers, voters also backed anti-AI candidates, electing officials vowing crackdowns in key states building out the most data center capacity in the US. summary: For the past few decades, the vast majority of U.S. startup funding has consistently gone to companies in blue states or purple states, where Democrats control all or some statewide offices.
